message.content:
The ocean usually looks **blue**—that’s because water absorbs colors from the red end of the spectrum more strongly than those on the blue side, so when sunlight hits the surface most of what we see is scattered back as blue wavelengths.  

In reality, its hue changes depending on depth, angle of view, weather, time of day, and surrounding environment:

| Condition | Typical Appearance |
|-----------|--------------------|
| Deep open waters | Bright turquoise‑to‑deep‑navy blue |
| Shallow coastal areas | Greenish‑teal or even yellow/amber where algae or sand reflect light |
| Overcast skies | Duller gray‑green tones |
| Sunset/sunrise | Warm orange/pink hues along horizons |

So while “sea” often evokes a vivid blue image, the actual color varies widely across different settings.
